lessons.title: Planning: Scope, WBS & Schedule
lessons.content:
KEY CONCEPTS: The Scope Statement defines what IS and IS NOT included — explicit exclusions prevent scope creep. The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposes deliverables into work packages small enough to estimate and assign (the 8/80 rule: no package smaller than 8 hours or larger than 80). Dependencies: Finish-to-Start (most common), Start-to-Start, Finish-to-Finish. The Critical Path is the longest chain of dependent tasks — it determines minimum project duration; delays here delay everything.

WORKED EXAMPLE: Building a website: WBS decomposes into Design → Frontend → Backend → Integration → Testing → Launch. Frontend and Backend can run in parallel (no dependency), but Integration cannot start until both finish. The critical path runs through whichever of the two takes longer.

PRACTICE: 1) Write a scope statement with 3 explicit exclusions. 2) Build a WBS with at least 8 work packages. 3) Map dependencies and identify the critical path.
